title: Galaxy Types: The Hubble Tuning Fork
welcome_lead: Spiral, elliptical, irregular — the morphology of galaxies.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: spirals, ellipticals, irregulars and Hubble's classification.
final_note: Galaxy shape correlates with star formation and dynamics.

concepts.def: Disk galaxy with arms — class S.
Smooth, featureless ellipsoid — class E0 to E7.
Galaxy without a clear shape — class Irr.
Spiral with a central bar — class SB.
Transition class with a disk but no spiral arms — S0.

walkthroughs.body_html: Ellipticals (E) are old, gas-poor and red. Spirals (S, SB) have gas, dust, blue arms and ongoing star formation. Irregulars (Irr) lack symmetry — often dwarfs or interacting systems.
Edwin Hubble's tuning fork (1926) places ellipticals on the handle (E0 round to E7 elongated), then splits into ordinary spirals (Sa-Sc) and barred spirals (SBa-SBc), joined by lenticular S0.
Sa and SBa have tight arms and big bulges; Sc and SBc have loose arms and small bulges. The Milky Way is a barred spiral, often classed SBbc.
